questions.text: A request declares support for an MCP extension. What does that declaration establish for authorization?

options.A: The client may use every tool that mentions the extension.
options.B: The self-reported clientInfo becomes an authenticated principal.
options.C: The client can process that feature; access still requires principal and resource policy checks.
options.D: The server can skip argument validation for requests using the extension.

questions.explanation: Capabilities declare protocol compatibility. Authorization must independently bind an authenticated principal to the tool, resource, and arguments.

questions.text: A gateway hides a changed descriptor from tools/list, but accepts direct calls to its qualified name. Which change closes the admission gap?

options.A: Recheck the current descriptor against admission policy before dispatching the call.
options.B: Hide the tool description while leaving the handler callable.
options.C: Automatically approve the new digest whenever a direct call arrives.
options.D: Require a familiar clientInfo.name in place of checking the descriptor.

questions.explanation: Discovery filtering does not enforce dispatch. The execution boundary must refuse a changed or unapproved descriptor before the handler runs.

questions.text: descriptor_digest uses json.dumps(tool, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")) before hashing. Two descriptors differ only in dictionary key insertion order. What does the function produce?

options.A: Different digests, because dictionary insertion order is always hashed.
options.B: An exception, because sorted JSON cannot contain nested objects.
options.C: Different digests, because separators randomize the output.
options.D: The same digest, because sorted keys produce the same serialized content.

questions.explanation: Sorting object keys canonicalizes insertion-order differences, including nested dictionaries. Actual descriptor value changes still change the serialized content.
